reply.text:
I'd want to see your actual long runs before giving you a plan, so let me pull them up. Nothing is logged for runs or a program yet, so I'm going on general coaching here.

Legs fading in the last mile usually means the long run is too fast early, or the weekly base underneath it is too small. Start the long run slower than feels necessary, easy enough that you could hold a conversation, and keep it to about one run a week that is longer than the rest. Add a couple of easy runs through the week so the long one isn't carrying all your mileage, and grow total distance gradually rather than jumping the long run.

Strength work for legs helps too, since single-leg moves, calves and hamstrings tend to be what gives out late. Fueling and sleep the day before matter more than people expect.

If you tell me your race or distance goal and how many days a week you can run, I can have the app build you a plan around it.
